 Key Takeaways from “2027-28 FAFSA and Financial Aid Information for High School Counselors” Webinar
 Nov 5, 2026 | Events , Initiatives 
 To help students and families navigate the financial aid process and complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid ( FAFSA ), school counselors need updated information, guidance, and resources.
 On October 29, 2026, the Florida College Access Network (FCAN) in partnership with the Florida Association of Student Financial Aid Administrators ( FASFAA ), and the Florida Department of Education’s Office of Student Financial Assistance ( OSFA ) hosted a webinar, led by Dr. Karemah Campbell-Mansell, Director of the Office of Student Financial Assistance at the University of Central Florida ( UCF ), to ensure counselors are equipped to serve their students with this key step in the college-going process.
 What is the FAFSA? 
 Students interested in receiving financial aid including grants, loans, and work study, should complete the FAFSA in their senior year of high school and every year they plan on enrolling in classes. This can help reduce college costs that may otherwise prevent students from continuing their education after high school.
 The form collects information to calculate the Student Aid Index (SAI), which colleges use to determine financial aid eligibility.
 Each college and university establishes its own FAFSA priority filing date, however, students should complete the FAFSA as early as possible to receive maximum consideration for available financial aid.
 Key Information: 
 The FAFSA is expected to be available by October 1 each year.
 Students and parents must create their own FSA ID.
 The 2027-2028 FAFSA uses financial information from two years prior.
 Students attending college during summer 2027 may need to complete both the 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 FAFSA applications depending on their enrollment.
 The FAFSA is available in English and Spanish, with assistance available in other languages.
 FAFSA Deadlines, Corrections, and Financial Aid Offers 
 Most Florida institutions are expected to release financial aid packages around March, although timelines differ by institution. If a student needs to make a correction to their submitted FAFSA, they should log into their account and resubmit to ensure accurate information is provided.
 For additional financial aid opportunities, students can visit their college’s website to discover institutional scholarships, application requirements, and deadlines.
 FCAN is also developing a common scholarship application portal that plans to serve students throughout Florida. In the meantime, access FCAN’s local scholarship resources page .
 Federal financial aid opportunities include: 
 Federal Pell Grant: Provides need-based grant assistance determined primarily through the Student Aid Index.
 Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant (FSEOG): Provides additional grant assistance to students with significant financial need. Funding is limited, making early FAFSA submission important.
 TEACH Grant: Supports eligible students pursuing certain education programs and teaching careers in high-need areas. If grant requirements are not fulfilled, the award converts to a loan.
 Federal Work-Study: Allows eligible students to earn money through employment while attending college.
 Federal Direct Student Loans: Provide students with the opportunity to borrow money to help cover educational expenses.
 Florida Bright Futures Scholarship 
 Bright Futures remains one of Florida’s most important scholarship opportunities. The two award levels, Florida Academic Scholars and Florida Medallion Scholars, each have their own criteria, requirements and eligibility:
 Florida Academic Scholars: Provides 100% of tuition and applicable fees at eligible state institutions, with up to 120 funded credit hours.
 Florida Medallion Scholars: Provides 75% of the applicable tuition and fee amount at eligible state institutions.
 Students should keep track of their GPA, coursework, standardized test scores, and volunteer or paid work hours. To be considered, students must complete the Florida Financial Aid Application by August 31 of their high school graduation year.
 Florida FAFSA Challenge 
 FCAN’s Florida FAFSA Challenge , a statewide initiative running through March 31, encourages schools and districts to increase their FAFSA completion rates by at least 5%. Those with the highest FAFSA completion rates and the most improvement will be recognized at the Talent Strong Florida Summit in May 2027 in Orlando.
 To help, FCAN provides the First Look Dashboard that allows schools and districts to monitor FAFSA completion progress with a more comprehensive dashboard coming in the new year.
 Encourage FAFSA Completion 
 Early preparation, accurate information, and consistent guidance are essential to helping students and families navigate the financial aid process.
 School counselors are a critical part of ensuring students understand their options and have the resources they need to pursue postsecondary education. Get started today at studentaid.gov .
